rejected.rationale: The reviewer's drop stands. Its own probe (ReviewProbeExpiredPresentedCopyTest) is green on current code: the JDK rejects the expired presented self-signed copy with certificate_expired (PKIX validity check failed), the proxy answers 502 CONNECT_FAILED and the backend gets 0 request bytes, which is what FR-PROXY-022 ('chain still validated (signature and validity period)') and SEC-PROXY-005 require. Execution disproves the suspected trusted-certificate shortcut bypass.

The reviewer's drop stands. The probe shows that a single caching SSLContext resumes the TLS 1.3 session with the same creation time (1795185017685 both), so the oracle 'second.getCreationTime() > first.getCreationTime()' in fr_PROXY_022_AC3_eachConnectionThroughTrustCertificatesRunsAFullHandshake does detect resumption. The test is not vacuous.

Speculative flakiness with no execution evidence. shortLived() (ProxyTrustCertificatesTest.java:1007-1016) uses -startdate -86390S -validity 1, so about 10 s are left, and it runs c.checkValidity() right after creation. The suite is green locally. This is a test-timing concern, not a functional defect claim, so it is not a residual. Nothing here breaks an AC.

Speculative timing and port-reuse races in GatewayEndToEndTest with no reproduction ('command: none'). The tests are green. This is a test-robustness opinion, not a proven defect, and not a functional defect of the product code.

This concerns the wording and completeness of a prose fixture list in a test-class javadoc. Every symbol it names exists. It is not a code defect, and the review-fix loop does not edit prose-only comments for completeness.

This is intended behavior. FR-PROXY-022 AC-4 (22.reverse-proxy.srs.md) requires IllegalArgumentException at the call for 'a block whose base64 or DER does not parse', and TrustedCertificates.java:76-87 deliberately requires the block to be exactly one DER certificate (getEncoded() equality, which also rejects trailing bytes; see VE-4 _aBlockWhoseDerHasTrailingBytesThrowsIllegalArgumentException). The finding comes from static reading only, and a non-DER (BER) certificate block falls under the specified rejection. RFC 7468 lets PEM carry BER, but the SRS deliberately narrows input to DER.
